run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Between 13:49:24Z and ~14:54Z on 2026-11-20, the payment-api container in namespace app-100a (pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-qsfjd, deployment payment-api-100a) logged database connection-pool exhaustion: pool_size 20 with all 20 connections active, waiting_requests up to 46 and acquire waits up to 26.8 s, error ConnectionPoolExhausted DB_CONN_001 at PaymentService.processPayment()/DatabasePool.acquire(). Its own DB-query timing rose from 18-88 ms baseline samples (11:21-13:17) to 1252-4953 ms during the episode, and its /healthz handler returned 503 'Health check failed - database unreachable' (5.0-9.7 s response) at 13:57:29, 14:01:50 and 14:44:44; by 15:01-15:15 query samples were back at 20-77 ms. Some payments still succeeded during the episode (323-389 ms), so the pod degraded rather than fully failed. The deepest observable cause is the database dependency's latency/unreachability, but the database is not a cluster object with logs or metrics I could see, so the trigger behind the pool exhaustion is unverified; I also could not read the app's DB/pool configuration (mounted Secret). Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run, and no Kubernetes event from 2026-11-20 was retained, so this is a partial conclusion with the database-side cause and the incident-time K8s state recorded as gaps.

claims.text: The payment-api pod's own logs show pool exhaustion starting at 13:49:24Z: 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 27, wait_time_ms 17653, and again at 13:50:55Z with waiting_requests 34, wait_time_ms 19706; at 13:50:55Z it also logged 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use', error_code DB_CONN_001, stack 'at PaymentService.processPayment()/at DatabasePool.acquire()'.

The application's own DB-query durations degraded by roughly one to two orders of magnitude: samples of 'Database query executed' read 18, 30, 57, 61, 65, 75, 76, 88 ms between 11:21:45Z and 13:17:12Z, then 1252 ms at 13:50:55Z, 3106 ms at 14:28:27Z, 4953 ms at 14:30:57Z, 4472 ms at 14:37:32Z, 2355 ms at 14:43:57Z, and returned to 20, 40, 41, 54, 77 ms at 15:01:00Z-15:15:23Z.

The pod reported failing health checks on its own /healthz endpoint: status_code 503 with message 'Health check failed - database unreachable' and response_time_ms 5009 at 13:57:29Z, 9684 at 14:01:50Z and 6354 at 14:44:44Z.

Queuing peaked well above the pool size: waiting_requests 46 with wait_time_ms 26398 at 14:30:57Z, waiting_requests 25 with 20933 ms at 14:32:51Z, and waiting_requests 21 with 26789 ms at 14:43:57Z, while active_connections stayed at the pool_size of 20 in every returned line.

The ERROR-level log count for namespace app-100a first becomes non-zero at the 13:49:24Z evaluation point of a 10-minute count_over_time series and the ERROR series' last non-zero point is 14:53:48Z; the latest ERROR line returned by a 14:40Z-15:10Z query is at 14:44:44Z.

Payment processing was degraded, not stopped: 'Payment processed successfully' lines with processing_time_ms 468 at 13:31:51Z, 389 at 14:07:40Z and 323 at 14:09:43Z appear inside or at the edge of the degraded period.

Deployment payment-api-100a (revision 1) runs a single container 'payment-api' with image python:3.9-slim, command python /app/app-direct-push.py, env containing only HOSTNAME (from fieldRef metadata.name), a livenessProbe httpGet /healthz on port 8080 (period 10s, failureThreshold 3) and memory limit 256Mi; the application script is mounted from a Secret volume, so its DB/pool settings are not readable.

At query time the only payment-api-100a pod is payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-qsfjd, which is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState; it was created 2026-11-21T04:35:02Z by ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 after the Deployment event 'Scaled up replica set payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 from 0 to 1' at 2026-11-21T04:35:01Z - i.e. roughly 14.8 hours after the incident, not during it.

The pod recreation is part of a cluster-wide restart after the incident: the returned app-100a events span only 2026-11-21T04:34:37Z-04:35:02Z (loki pod created 04:34:39Z, payment-api pod container started 04:35:02Z), and many kube-system and otel-demo containers show a previous terminated instance finished at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and restartCount 1.
At query time the node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False.
Namespace app-100a contains only two ConfigMaps, kube-root-ca.crt and loki-config; none holds payment-api database, connection-pool or fault-injection settings.
A sum-by-job log-count query across all namespaces for 13:30Z-14:30Z returned a single log stream, job="payment-api" - no database or other dependency logs are present in this Loki source.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap contains fault-injection flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), both with state ENABLED and defaultVariant 'off' in the ConfigMap as read at 2026-11-21T04:37Z.

Most likely mechanism: the payment-api pod's fixed 20-connection database pool saturated because database query latency jumped from tens of milliseconds to 1.2-5.0 seconds, queuing up to 46 waiting acquisition requests (17-27 s waits) and pushing /healthz to 503; the latency increase, not the pool size, is the trigger. This remains a hypothesis because the database side is not observable.

Candidate deeper cause: the external database itself was degraded or intermittently unreachable during 13:49Z-14:54Z, as the application's own /healthz message 'database unreachable' suggests, but no DB pod, Service, metric series or log stream is visible, so the responsible database object cannot be identified or named.

Candidate contributing cause: a 20-connection pool with up to 46 queued requests may be undersized for this workload, or the pool/DB settings may have been changed before 13:45Z; the pool_size value comes from the application's own log line and its configuration lives in a mounted Secret that cannot be read, so this is unverified.

The otel-demo flagd fault-injection flags were considered and are not supported as the cause of the payment-api-100a errors: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable read 'off' in the ConfigMap and are described for 'the payment service' (a different otel-demo entity), and the payment-api-100a pod template wires no flagd provider or flagd-related env (only HOSTNAME). Caveat: the ConfigMap state was read after the incident, so its value at 13:45Z is unknown.

Node-level resource exhaustion is not evidenced: the only node is Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False at query time, and the payment-api container's memory limit is 256Mi while its restartCount is 0 with an empty lastState.

gaps: No metrics: every Prometheus query attempted in this Run (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or saturation series exist for payment-api-100a or its database; this also means missing metric series are unknown, not zero.

No traces: traces_list_services, traces_search (service 'payment') and traces_search (service 'frontend') all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level evidence of the database call or of caller impact was obtainable.

No Kubernetes evidence from 2026-11-20: the retained events span only 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z-04:35:02Z, all app-100a events concern the Nov 21 pod recreation, so nothing shows whether the pod restarted, was killed or was rescheduled around 13:45Z on Nov 20.

The database dependency is not observable: no DB pod or Service exists (only 'payment' in otel-demo, a different service), Loki returns only the job="payment-api" stream, and no DB-side metric or log was found, so the object that caused the query-latency increase cannot be named.

The payment-api DB/pool configuration is in a Secret-mounted script volume (Secret not readable), so pool_size 20, DB host and timeouts are seen only as values quoted in application log lines; whether they changed before the incident is unknown.

Onset precision is limited by log sampling: the first returned ERROR line is 13:49:24Z while the question cites ~13:45Z; the exact first failure between the last normal sample and 13:49:24Z is unknown.

Queries for ERROR-level lines before 13:49:00Z and after 15:00:00Z on 2026-11-20 returned no data (empty results, status no_data); that only shows those specific queries matched nothing and cannot establish absence of errors, and no WARN-level lines or retry/failover/reset messages were returned either.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so any infrastructure or database-side change around 13:45Z cannot be checked.

The current cluster state (pod names, deployment revision, node conditions) is the state at query time 2026-11-21T04:36Z, roughly 14.8 hours after the incident, and cannot prove the state during the incident.
next_steps: Obtain database-side telemetry (DB server slow-query/latency, connection counts, availability) and the DB endpoint's identity for payment-api-100a, which would confirm or refute the database-latency hypothesis.

Inspect the Secret that supplies /app/app-direct-push.py and the DB settings (pool size, timeouts, DB host) through an authorized channel, to see whether pool sizing or a config value changed before 13:45Z.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access for the 2026-11-20 13:30Z-15:00Z window to compare payment-api-100a's error rate and latency against an earlier baseline and to check whether any caller of payment-api saw failures.
Check change history for app-100a, DNS/CoreDNS and the database tier around 2026-11-20 13:45Z, since cluster events from that day have expired.
